query: What features can be extracted to train a model to predict a review's score?

per_column.name: sentiment_polarity
per_column.rationale: Overall polarity of the review is essentially a proxy/restatement of the score; positive/negative sentiment is what the star rating encodes, so it leaks the outcome rather than predicting it from independent signal.

per_column.name: product_quality_assessment
per_column.rationale: An excellent/poor/defective quality judgment extracted from the same review text is a direct evaluative summary of the score; it near-deterministically tracks the rating and constitutes leakage.

per_column.name: taste_flavor_experience
per_column.rationale: Excellent/poor taste is an evaluative sentiment aspect derived from the review itself; it mirrors the reviewer's satisfaction and thus the score, not an external predictor.

per_column.name: sensory_assessment
per_column.rationale: Pleasant/unpleasant sensory verdict is another aspect-level restatement of the reviewer's evaluation, strongly collinear with the star rating.

per_column.name: repeat_purchase_intent
per_column.rationale: Willingness to repurchase is a canonical expression of satisfaction that co-occurs with and encodes the rating; extracted from the review, it leaks the outcome.

per_column.name: price_value_assessment
per_column.rationale: Good/poor/overpriced value is an evaluative judgment mined from the review text and moves directly with the score; it is a restatement rather than an independent price feature.

per_column.name: product_defect_or_issue
per_column.rationale: A flag that the review mentions a defect is a strong negative-evaluation signal drawn from the same text, effectively encoding low scores; leakage, not external predictor.

per_column.name: expectation_fit
per_column.rationale: Exceeded/unmet expectations is virtually the definition of satisfaction and maps almost one-to-one onto the star rating; classic outcome restatement.

per_column.name: comparison_to_alternatives
per_column.rationale: Favorable/unfavorable-vs-competitor is an evaluative sentiment aspect extracted from the review, tightly coupled to the reviewer's overall verdict and hence the score.

per_column.name: health_dietary_concern
per_column.rationale: Whether the review raises a health/dietary topic is a content/topic feature that is not itself an evaluative verdict; it can carry weak predictive signal about the score without being a restatement of it, though it borders on aspect extraction.

judge.rationale: Nine of the ten added columns are aspect-level or overall evaluative judgments (sentiment, quality, taste, sensory, value, defect, expectations, repurchase, competitor comparison) mined from the same review text whose score is being predicted. These are near-deterministic restatements/leakage of the reviewer's satisfaction, so a model using them would 'predict' the score only because the columns already encode it. Only health_dietary_concern is a genuine topical feature that lies outside the evaluative outcome, and it offers modest signal at best. As a set they provide little legitimate predictive leverage beyond leakage.
